checks.area: recount of blocks, views and windows
evidence: 335 unique inventory blocks: 140 treadmill, 136 stairs, 40 sit-stand, 19 crouch.

Views = 15,825 under the converter's rule (reconvert_mblue_normalized.py lines 61-67): gait and stair blocks emit one view per side cycle; STS and crouch blocks emit one observation per left cycle, with the right side as contra. All 59 such blocks have bilateral_clocks_exactly_equal true.

The inventory itself holds 16,418 side-cycles, so 593 right STS/crouch cycles are carried as contra columns. The handoff's chain line 'inventory (335 blocks, 15,825 views)' is shorthand for this, not a literal inventory count.
Conversion and readback records cover the same 335 blocks, with per-block observations equal to these views. The readback sum is 15,825 and its maximum error is 1.8e-15.
764 recovered windows (426 right, 338 left) across exactly 136 stair blocks. Each subject/condition's expected_windows equals its single matched candidate.

checks.result: pass (all 136 blocks, not only a sample)
checks.evidence: For every stair block I parsed the IDs with my own regex. Retained IDs equal the recovered (side, curve index) windows. Omitted IDs equal the other leg at the same columns. Per block, left_unchanged equals all left views, and right_changed plus right_unchanged equals all right views. Totals: treadmill 6,858 left unchanged, 6,842 right changed, 4 right unchanged; stairs 764 and 764 unchanged; sit-stand 404 and crouch 189 left unchanged. Every changed block lists the same 14 pelvis/segment columns, and all_other_columns_exactly_preserved is true.

14 bindings recomputed by me all equal the current bytes: inventory to conversion and recovery, baseline and corrected summaries to preservation, rebuild to readback and correction, recovery to correction, and all 7 scope-gate inputs. checks.result: not explained in receipts; worker's statement accurate
evidence: No receipt records a per-view reason; preservation gives counts only.

The three blocks have more right than left cycles: AB04/exo/decline_10deg r-l = 2 (1 unchanged), AB05/bare/decline_5deg r-l = 7 (2 unchanged), AB11/bare/incline_10deg r-l = 2 (1 unchanged). Among all 140 treadmill blocks, unchanged right views occur only where r-l >= 2 (3 of 7 such blocks; 0 in the 133 blocks with r-l <= 1).

That pattern fits right cycles lacking left-clock overlap ('missing overlap preserved'), but the receipts cannot prove it, because pre-fix values are not recorded per view. It stays a not-checked item for the full-byte job or a targeted probe.

checks.area: full-byte job spec vs guarded_launcher envelope
evidence: validate_spec on the spec as written raises SpecError (bindings) because of the TO_BIND_AFTER_REVIEW placeholder. That is expected and disclosed.

With the placeholder replaced by a dummy hash, validate_spec passes in-process. timeout 3600, kill_after 30, poll 15, memory 3584/2816 and 2048/2048, address space 768 MiB and disk 5120 MiB all sit at the PM-01 limits.

Defect: run_job hashes bindings relative to cwd, the repository root. The four receipt keys ('mblue_reference_corrected_full_20261021/correction_summary.json' etc.) do not exist there, so the launch would be refused with binding_mismatch. With the converted_datasets/reconversion_v2/ prefix, all four recorded hashes equal the current files. The audit note claims the prefix is used.

Feasibility note: importing pyarrow under RLIMIT_AS 768 MiB hung (timed out) without the thread environment. With the launcher's THREAD_ENV (ARROW_NUM_THREADS=1 etc.), import and a small read succeed at 768 MiB. So stage 2 is feasible only through the launcher, and the pilot must confirm it.
